spec.description: IPS, Trust Cache, and AI Decisions Now also includes Layer-1 process health (CPU, memory, uptime) alongside the existing IPS mitigation, Continuous-Learning False-Positive Engine, and Ollama SOC transparency panels.

spec.title: 🛡️ IPS Mitigations & Tarpitting
spec.description: Section header. The three tiles below show what's ACTIVELY isolated right now, in real time.

options.content: Real-time state of the Intrusion Prevention System.

spec.title: Confirmed Threats (Hard-Stop Bypass)
spec.description: How many alerts were stopped at Stage 1 — the deterministic hard-stop security filter that runs BEFORE any ML model, on signals like a confirmed honeypot hit or a Tier-5 threat-intel match. These bypass the false-positive engine entirely and always fire as confirmed threats (see fp_engine.py: 'hard-stop signals fired → CONFIRMED THREAT despite trust cache hit').

spec.title: LGBM Model Status
spec.description: Is the LightGBM ONNX false-positive classifier model currently loaded and serving Stage 2 of the CL-AFPE pipeline? Red means Stage 2 scoring is unavailable and the engine is relying only on Stage 1 hard-stops and Stage 3 FastEmbed similarity.

spec.title: 📜 AFPE Suppressed/Muted Log
spec.description: Every alert the false-positive engine has AUTONOMOUSLY suppressed, with its exact reasoning — this is the transparency guarantee: nothing is ever silently discarded. 'Type' tells you which of the 3 suppression paths fired: TRUST_CACHE_HIT (instant, domain was already immunized), AUTONOMOUS_FP_SUPPRESSED (passed the full Stage 1→2→3 pipeline and cleared fp_combined_suppress_threshold = 0.8), or OPERATOR_MARKED_FALSE_POSITIVE (you corrected it manually). PREREQUISITE: this panel needs a Loki scrape target for state/autonomous_muted.jsonl with job="home_ids_muted" — see the setup panel below if this table is empty.

spec.expr: {job="home_ids_muted"} | json ts="ts_human", type="type", confidence="confidence", reasons="reasons", domain="domain", risk_score="risk_score", device_ip="device.ip"

spec.title: 🤖 AI Reasoning & Tuning Transparency
spec.description: Two things happen here: (1) 'ollama_transparency' entries are Brain 3's full LLM reasoning for every alert it batch-analyzed — model used, its classification, confidence, reasoning, recommended action, and whether the deterministic threat-intel guardrail (validator_passed) approved or overrode it. (2) 'afpe_tuning' entries, if present, would represent autonomous threshold retuning — this event type was not found in the reviewed engine source during the Version 7.0 audit, so treat rows of that type as unverified/legacy until confirmed against your actual deployed code.

spec.expr: {job="home_ids_alerts"} |= "ollama_transparency" or "afpe_tuning" | json ts="timestamp", device_ip="device.ip", risk="risk", model="model", classification="response.classification", ai_confidence="response.confidence", reason="response.reason", action="response.recommended_action", validator_passed="validator_passed"

spec.title: Active L2 ARP Tarpits
spec.description: Devices currently trapped by the Layer-2 Scapy ARP/NDP tarpit. This is usually the FASTEST mitigation to take effect since it needs no external API — a device can be tarpitted even if your router or Pi-hole integration is down.

spec.title: Active WAN Isolations
spec.description: Devices currently cut off from WAN access via the Fritz!Box TR-064 integration (Layer 3). Local LAN access is deliberately left intact so you can still SSH in and remediate the machine.

spec.title: Active Pi-Hole Blocks
spec.description: Devices/domains currently under an active Pi-hole DNS block (Layer 7). This is a live gauge of enforcement, not the lifetime counter — compare against the 'Lifetime Threats Blocked' tile on the Overview dashboard to see cumulative vs. currently-active blocks.

spec.title: 🧠 Autonomous False-Positive Elimination (AFPE)
spec.description: Section header for the Continuous-Learning False-Positive Engine (CL-AFPE) metrics below — the system that keeps Home-IDS from crying wolf over your smart TV's firmware checks.

options.content: Metrics tracking the dynamic Trust Cache and AI overrides.

spec.title: AFPE Total Evaluations
spec.description: Total alerts that crossed alert_threshold and were routed into the false-positive engine for a suppress/confirm decision — the denominator for everything below (Stage 1 Hardstops, Suppressed, Confidence Score).

spec.title: AFPE Alerts Suppressed
spec.description: How many of those evaluations were autonomously suppressed as false positives (Stage 2/3 combined confidence >= fp_combined_suppress_threshold = 0.8, from config.yaml). The gap between 'Total Evaluations' and this number is how many alerts actually reached you as real threats.

spec.title: Trust Cache Size
spec.description: How many unique domains are currently held in the 14-day trust cache (fp_revoke_action_ttl_seconds-adjacent TTL logic). Queries matching this cache skip the ML pipeline entirely for near-zero-latency suppression — this is Brain 2's short-term memory.

spec.title: AFPE Confidence Score
spec.description: The combined Stage 2 (LightGBM) + Stage 3 (FastEmbed) confidence that an alert is a false positive. Thresholds now reflect the real config.yaml values: below 0.55 (fp_combined_uncertain_threshold) is treated as still-a-real-threat territory (🔴), 0.55-0.79 is the 'uncertain, tagged low-confidence' band (🟡), and 0.8+ (fp_combined_suppress_threshold) is confidently auto-suppressed (🟢).

spec.title: 🔌 Prerequisite: Wire Up the Missing Loki Stream
spec.description: The exact promtail config needed to make the AFPE Suppressed/Muted Log panel actually receive data.

options.content:
**Why the AFPE Suppressed/Muted Log panel above might be empty.** Home-IDS writes suppressed-alert audit entries to `state/autonomous_muted.jsonl` — a SEPARATE file from `alerts.json`. The Promtail scrape config in INSTALL.md only ships `alerts.json` (job=`home_ids_alerts`) to Loki by default; `autonomous_muted.jsonl` isn't wired up unless you add a second scrape target. Add this to `/etc/promtail/config.yml` under `scrape_configs`, then `sudo systemctl restart promtail`:

```yaml
  - job_name: home_ids_muted
    static_configs:
      - targets: [localhost]
        labels:
          job: home_ids_muted
          __path__: /home/user/home_ids/state/autonomous_muted.jsonl
```

(Path assumes the standard project layout from INSTALL.md — adjust if yours differs.) Once wired up, the panel above will show every alert the false-positive engine silently resolved, with its exact reasoning — nothing is ever discarded without a trace.

spec.title: ⚙️ Engine CPU Usage
spec.description: CPU time consumed by the Home-IDS process itself (process_cpu_seconds_total, a standard metric automatically exposed by the prometheus_client library — confirmed in requirements.txt). Sustained high usage can slow down the 5-phase detection loop and delay alerting; compare against Alert Queue on the Overview dashboard if you suspect the engine is falling behind.

spec.title: 💾 Engine Memory (RSS)
spec.description: Resident memory used by the Home-IDS process (process_resident_memory_bytes). Grows with max_device_states and the size of your ML models — a slow, steady climb over days/weeks with no plateau can indicate a memory leak worth investigating.

spec.title: ⏱️ Engine Uptime
spec.description: How long the current Home-IDS process has been running without a restart (time() - process_start_time_seconds). Drops to zero unexpectedly = the service crashed and systemd restarted it — worth checking journalctl if this doesn't match your last intentional deploy/restart.

spec.title: 🧪 CL-AFPE 3-Stage Funnel (Evaluated → Hard-Stopped → Suppressed)
spec.description: Three CL-AFPE counters plotted together as a funnel: Total Evaluations (everything that crossed alert_threshold), Stage 1 Hardstops (bypassed straight to CONFIRMED THREAT on a honeypot/reputation hit — never even gets an FP chance), and Suppressed (autonomously resolved as false positives). The gap between Evaluations and (Hardstops + Suppressed) is what actually reached you as a real, unresolved alert — the smaller that gap relative to Evaluations, the quieter and more trustworthy your SOC feed is.

spec.title: 🩺 Subsystem Health
spec.description: Section header.

options.content: **What couldn't the system do, right now?** PHASE 30: this dashboard is titled "System Tuning, Healing & Health" but had zero general subsystem up/down visibility until this row -- Pi-hole/Zeek status lived on the Overview dashboard, and Suricata/Pi-hole-gravity had none anywhere. Consolidated here so every subsystem's health is in one glanceable place.

spec.title: 🦈 Suricata Health
spec.description: home_ids_suricata_scan_total's live success/error ratio over the last 30m -- see the Overview dashboard's identical panel for full description.

spec.title: 🌐 Pi-hole Gravity-List API Health
spec.description: Time since the last successful home_ids_pihole_gravity_last_success_timestamp -- see the Overview dashboard's identical panel for full description.

spec.title: Zeek Network Monitor
spec.description: home_ids_zeek_status -- reference copy of the Overview dashboard's identical panel, so Zeek's status is visible here alongside every other subsystem too.

spec.title: Pi-hole IPS
spec.description: home_ids_ips_pihole_status -- reference copy of the Overview dashboard's identical panel, so Pi-hole's status is visible here alongside every other subsystem too.
Caption for the subsystem status tiles below.

options.content: 🟢/ONLINE/ARMED = working right now. 🔴/OFFLINE/UNAVAILABLE = that specific layer is down -- the other containment layers keep working independently, hover any tile for exactly what to check.

spec.description: Caption for LGBM Model Status.

options.content: 🟢/LOADED = the LightGBM Stage-2 false-positive classifier is active. 🔴/UNAVAILABLE = FP suppression falls back to Stage 1 rules only -- more alerts, not fewer, so this failing is safe but noisier.

spec.description: Caption for the active-mitigation-count tiles below.

options.content: ✅ Clear = nothing of that kind is active right now (good). A number = that many devices currently under that containment.
Is the engine keeping up with live traffic, and did any automated block/isolate/tarpit action ever fail silently? These panels exist so a failure in the mitigation pipeline itself is never invisible.

spec.title: Pipeline Collector Lag
spec.description: Seconds between an event happening and the engine finishing processing it. Should stay near 0 -- a climbing value means the engine is falling behind live traffic and detections are delayed.

spec.title: Threat Intel Engine Ready
spec.description: 1 once ThreatIntel has completed at least one successful feed refresh. While this is 0, every TI lookup fails open (reads as 'clean') simply because no feed data has loaded yet -- distinguishing that cold-start state from 'genuinely checked, nothing found' is the entire point of this metric.

spec.title: FP Embedding Model Status
spec.description: Is the FastEmbed ONNX vector-similarity model (CL-AFPE Stage 3) loaded? If not, the false-positive engine falls back to Stages 1-2 only for every alert.

spec.title: Events Processed Rate
spec.description: DNS/network events per second flowing through the pipeline. A sudden drop to zero while devices are still active on the network usually means the collector (Pi-hole log tail or Zeek) has stalled, not that traffic actually stopped.

spec.title: IPS Mitigation Errors by Stage
spec.description: Failures encountered while trying to actually execute a block/isolate/unblock action, broken down by which integration failed (Pi-hole API, router webhook, etc). This should normally stay at zero -- any sustained rate here means automatic protection is not actually being applied even though the engine decided it should be.

spec.title: Domains Stuck In Retry Queue
spec.description: Pi-hole block commands that failed and are being retried. Anything sitting here for a long time (check the Pi-hole IPS health stat on the Main Overview dashboard too) means that specific domain is currently NOT actually blocked despite the engine deciding it should be.

spec.title: Domains Permanently Failed (Dead Letter)
spec.description: Domains that exhausted all retry attempts and were given up on -- these are NOT blocked and nothing will retry them automatically. If this list grows, the underlying Pi-hole connectivity problem needs a human to look at it.

spec.title: Lifetime Router Isolations
spec.description: Total number of times the router (Layer-3 WAN kill-switch) has been triggered to fully isolate a device, ever.

spec.title: Lifetime Tarpit Activations
spec.description: Total number of times the Layer-2 ARP/NDP tarpit has been triggered to trap a device, ever.

spec.title: Suricata: Time Since Last Success
spec.description: Suricata only runs during a reactive-capture burst, so gaps of hours between successes are normal (unlike the always-on jobs elsewhere on this dashboard) -- this is here so a burst that keeps triggering Suricata scans that keep failing doesn't go unnoticed.

spec.title: Pi-hole Gravity-List Lookup Volume
spec.description: How often threat_signals.py asks Pi-hole's gravity list whether a domain is a known CDN/telemetry domain, and whether those lookups are succeeding. A rate stuck at zero while devices are active suggests the gravity-list integration itself has stopped being consulted.
